name: Ludwig Prandtl
summary: German physicist and engineer, pioneer of modern fluid mechanics and aerodynamics.

name: Irmgard Fliigge-Lotz
summary: German-American mathematician and engineer, author of this reminiscence.

name: Wilhelm Fliigge
summary: German-American engineer and co-author of this reminiscence.

name: A. Betz
summary: German physicist and long-time colleague of Prandtl at Gottingen.

name: University of Gottingen
summary: German university where Prandtl held a professorship.

name: Kaiser-Wilhelm-Institut
summary: Research institute for fluid dynamics directed by Prandtl.

name: Aerodynamische Versuchsanstalt
summary: Financially independent wind tunnel facility associated with Prandtl's institute.

name: Institute for Applied Mechanics
summary: University institute where Prandtl started his work in Gottingen.

name: Mathematics Institute
summary: Institute building where Prandtl's seminars took place.

name: Rockefeller Foundation
summary: Foundation that provided funding for the Mathematics Institute building.

name: Ludwig Föppl
summary: Professor of mechanics, father of Mrs. Prandtl.

name: Mrs. Prandtl
summary: Wife of Ludwig Prandtl and daughter of Ludwig Föppl.

name: Tokyo
summary: City in Japan where Prandtl attended an engineering congress.

name: Mariaspring
summary: Coffee-garden restaurant near Gottingen visited by Prandtl's group.

name: A. Nädai
summary: Authority on plasticity and former assistant at Prandtl's institute.

name: W. Prager
summary: Assistant at the Institute for Applied Mechanics in the early 1930s.

name: A. Busemann
summary: Researcher who built the rotating laboratory at Gottingen.

name: Clark Millikan
summary: American scientist who spent a year at Gottingen before the Nazi years.

name: H. Reichardt
summary: Researcher who investigated turbulence in a big air channel.

name: L. v. Seebach
summary: Prandtl's long-time secretary.

name: F. Schultz-Grunow
summary: Professor in Aachen who handled consulting billing for Prandtl.

name: German Airforce
summary: Military organization that supported the Fluid Mechanics Institute after 1933.
